title: Migrating to and from Gemini
summary: This intermediate module enables learners to define a migration path, verify it against the relevant first-party documentation, and test whether an integration still meets its requirements. It also teaches learners to distinguish a source-record correction from a supported change to technical guidance.
objectives: Identify whether a proposed Gemini migration concerns an API interface, compatibility path, library, prompt behavior, data flow, or another integration boundary.
Build an evidence-backed mapping between the behavior required before and after a migration.
Design tests that reveal unsupported assumptions, behavioral differences, and failed rollback conditions.
Record source uncertainty without turning an unverified detail into technical guidance.

sections.title: What changed in this correction
paragraphs: The prior source record identified the module file itself, content/modules/google-gemini-practice/migrating-to-and-from-gemini.json, as an unregistered source that had never been verified. This correction replaces that unusable citation record with the first-party Google documentation listed in the sources array.

The old source title, old external URL, previous module text, and repository history were not supplied. Therefore, the identity of any external page that moved is UNKNOWN, the effect of that movement on technical guidance is UNKNOWN, and preservation of unaffected wording cannot be confirmed. No particular migration mechanism or technical change should be inferred from the source-record correction alone.

The replacement affects source provenance and the ability to locate relevant first-party guidance. It does not establish that a specific Gemini behavior changed. A technical correction requires comparison of the previous claim, the previous supporting page, and the current first-party page.
sections.callout: Treat an updated citation and updated technical behavior as separate findings. A new URL does not by itself prove that the documented behavior changed.

sections.title: Define the migration boundary
paragraphs: Migration can refer to different integration boundaries. It may concern an API interface, an OpenAI-compatible interface, a generative AI library, prompt behavior, data flow, model substitution, or another part of an application. The intended boundary is UNKNOWN until the existing integration and desired destination are described.

Begin by recording the current input, required output, error expectations, operational constraints, and behaviors that users depend on. Then state the destination and the reason for moving. This prevents a familiar interface from being mistaken for identical behavior.

Select documentation only after identifying the boundary. The general Gemini API documentation is the starting point for Gemini API behavior. Google's OpenAI compatibility documentation is relevant when that compatibility path is actually in scope. Google's migration guide is relevant when the integration uses a library or migration path covered by that guide.

sections.title: Build an evidence map
paragraphs: Create one record for each required behavior. Each record should name the requirement, identify where the current integration implements it, link to the first-party destination documentation, and define a test that can confirm the result.

Mark a destination detail UNKNOWN when the checked documentation does not establish it. Do not fill a gap by assuming that two similarly named operations have the same inputs, outputs, limits, or failure behavior.
Separate required behavior from optional improvement. A migration is easier to review when each required behavior has evidence and a test, while unrelated redesign work is deferred.
sections.callout: A compatibility path can reduce interface changes, but its exact supported behavior and limitations must be established from the current first-party documentation before use.

sections.title: Test before switching
paragraphs: Use representative inputs and expected properties rather than relying on a single successful example. Tests should cover ordinary requests, invalid inputs, expected failure handling, and any output properties the application depends on.

A generated response does not have to use identical wording to satisfy the same requirement. Compare properties that matter to the application, such as whether required information is present, whether the result can be processed, and whether failures are handled safely.

Define rollback conditions before switching. A rollback condition is an observable result that requires returning to the previous integration or stopping the migration. Preserve the previous path until the required tests pass and the rollback procedure has been exercised.

sections.title: Apply the process in both directions
paragraphs: The same evidence process applies when moving to Gemini and when moving from Gemini. Document the source behavior, identify the destination interface, map each required behavior, test the destination, and retain a rollback path.

Do not assume that reversing a completed migration reproduces the original integration. Prompts, data handling, validation rules, and application expectations may have changed after the first migration. Recreate the evidence map from the current state.

When moving to Gemini, use the relevant current Google documentation to establish Gemini-side behavior. When moving away from Gemini, use Google documentation to establish the behavior being replaced and the destination provider's first-party documentation to establish destination behavior. No destination provider is specified in this module, so destination-specific instructions are UNKNOWN and omitted.

sections.title: Record the review
paragraphs: For each technical claim, record the supporting page, the date it was checked, the behavior it supports, and the test connected to it. If a page moves, confirm that the replacement is controlled by the same first-party publisher and still supports the claim.

A redirect or replacement URL establishes where a document can now be found only after it is checked. It does not establish whether the document's technical content stayed the same. Compare the relevant content or an authoritative change record before changing technical guidance.

The current source check identifies first-party documentation locations, but live page contents and resolution could not be confirmed in the drafting environment. Current migration procedures, supported compatibility behavior, versions, names, keys, endpoints, and limitations are therefore UNKNOWN and are not asserted here.

questions.prompt: What does a replacement URL establish by itself?
choices: That all documented technical behavior changed
That all previous guidance remains technically correct
Only a possible new location, pending confirmation that the page is first-party and still supports the claim
That migration tests are no longer necessary
questions.explanation: The module separates citation location from technical behavior. A replacement location must be checked, and any technical change requires additional evidence.

questions.prompt: What should be done before selecting a migration mechanism?
choices: Assume the title identifies the required interface
Define the current integration boundary, required behavior, destination, and reason for moving
Treat similarly named operations as identical
questions.explanation: The module instructs learners to define the migration boundary and required behavior before choosing documentation or a mechanism.

questions.prompt: How should a destination detail be handled when checked documentation does not establish it?
choices: Infer it from a similar interface
Mark it UNKNOWN and do not turn it into technical guidance
Present it as a standard default
Exclude it from testing but continue to depend on it
questions.explanation: The evidence-map section says to mark unsupported destination details UNKNOWN rather than filling gaps with assumptions.

questions.prompt: Why should a migration away from Gemini use a new evidence map instead of simply reversing an earlier migration?
choices: Because first-party documentation is unnecessary when reversing a migration
Because the integration and its requirements may have changed since the earlier migration
Because tests apply only when moving to Gemini
questions.explanation: The module explains that prompts, data handling, validation rules, and application expectations may have changed, so the current state must be documented and tested.
